title: World models that survive novel interventions

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a learned model of how a system responds when someone changes it. Starting from low-level observations such as images, waveforms or text, the learner would discover useful high-level causal variables and the mechanisms connecting them. With only a limited budget of real interventions, it would then predict the outcomes of previously unseen interventions within an explicitly defined class. This joins two problems that are often treated separately: extracting meaningful variables from sensory data and learning what happens when those variables or their mechanisms are changed.

A plausible video continuation or an accurate prediction under familiar conditions would not by itself demonstrate this capability. The model must support causal statements about specified changes to the system, including changes absent from its training interventions. Its learned variables need not reproduce a human vocabulary or a unique hidden graph, but they must preserve the causal distinctions needed for those predictions. What counts as successful recovery therefore depends on the intended abstraction, identifying assumptions and intervention class.

significance.text: Statistical association alone does not determine what happens under intervention. If a learned world model remained accurate under a specified class of unseen interventions, it could support planning through imagined outcomes, selection of informative experiments and evaluation of policies using more than correlational evidence. The consequential advance would be the ability to learn intervention-faithful simulators from observations and limited experiments without requiring a person to specify every mechanism beforehand.

Video prediction, latent dynamics optimized for a reward and fluent answers to counterfactual questions can all be useful, but none alone establishes this stronger capability. Performance under a training policy does not establish reliability when an action changes the distribution or mechanism being modeled. Conversely, a reward-trained model is not automatically incapable of causal prediction: its evidence must be assessed against the interventions and conditions actually tested.

Synthesis: the impact would remain bounded by the mechanisms, intervention classes and uncertainty guarantees that the model supports. A successful result would not establish unrestricted transfer to arbitrary systems, nor would it automatically produce autonomous scientific discovery. Discovering a compact new empirical law and confirming it experimentally would require further capabilities beyond reliable prediction of intervention outcomes.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central challenge is to learn causal variables and mechanisms from sensory observations while making efficient use of interventions. Conventional causal inference commonly begins with specified variables; perceptual learning must first decide which aspects of a complex observation matter. A representation that captures statistical dependence may still fail to preserve the distinctions needed to predict how a system changes under intervention.

Identification requires assumptions or informative data: different causal explanations can otherwise fit the available observations. The 2021 review discusses restricted positive results, including theoretical sufficiency of sparse mechanism shifts under suitable training data. Those results prevent a blanket claim that useful guarantees are unavailable. The unresolved question for this innovation is whether assumptions strong enough to identify the relevant causal structure can also fit realistic sensory observations, a limited intervention budget and the desired breadth of intervention prediction.

Synthesis: a convincing solution would have to connect three engineering capabilities. It must extract stable abstractions from changing observations, connect available physical actions to the interventions represented by those abstractions, and predict outcomes when familiar mechanisms are changed in unfamiliar ways. It must also recognize when the available evidence cannot distinguish competing explanations and express uncertainty usefully. The supplied evidence does not establish whether this combined capability has been achieved by November 2026.

current_state.text: Schölkopf, Locatello, Bauer, Ke, Kalchbrenner, Goyal and Bengio’s Toward Causal Representation Learning appeared in Proceedings of the IEEE in May 2021, volume 109(5), pages 612–634; the supplied research dates its arXiv preprint to 22 February 2021. The reviewed abstract identifies discovery of high-level causal variables from low-level observations as a central research problem. Section II distinguishes statistical association models from models that support intervention predictions, and later sections discuss interventional world models, restricted theoretical results and intervention-aware benchmarks. These establish a research agenda and partial foundations, not completion of the proposed innovation. The retained IEEE page contains the abstract rather than the full article; the preprint extraction includes substantive main sections but truncates the references.

The supplied research describes DreamerV3 as a positive component: learning a world model and improving behavior through imagined futures. It attributes to a Nature paper dated 2 April 2025, volume 640, pages 647–653, the result of collecting diamonds in Minecraft from scratch without human data or curricula, and characterizes the evaluated domains as simulated and resettable. These details remain unverified in the supplied evidence review: the retained PubMed response contains only a cookie notice, with no article title, authors, abstract or results. Consequently, neither these reported achievements nor the earlier characterization of DreamerV3 as the strongest positive component can be confirmed here. This access failure does not show that the reported results are false; it prevents using them as verified evidence of progress toward the complete target.

The T2VPhysBench preprint, arXiv:2505.00337v1, dated 1 May 2025, reports human evaluation of ten video-generation models. Their overall average physical-consistency scores range from 0.19 to 0.42. Its introductory assertion that scores fall below 0.60 across every law category conflicts with Table 2, where Qingying scores 0.63 on phenomenon principles. The overall averages support a narrower conclusion about poor performance among the models evaluated at that time; they do not support the stronger every-category statement or a claim about all models in 2026.

T2VPhysBench measures human judgments of physical consistency in generated videos. It does not directly test discovery of causal variables or prediction under held-out interventions on a system. Its results therefore illustrate limitations of visual generation without establishing the status of causal world models as a whole. The supplied review assessed the retained textual paper, which was untruncated; figures and videos were not independently inspected to verify physical behavior.

Evidence boundary: the supplied materials motivate the innovation and document restricted foundations and a dated video benchmark. They contain no freshness assessment establishing field-wide openness as of 1 November 2026. The complete capability is not demonstrated by this evidence, but the evidence also does not justify claiming that no qualifying method exists.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: evaluators would hide the causal graph and mechanisms of a complex simulated system. The learner would receive low-level observations and a capped intervention budget, then predict outcomes of evaluator-selected held-out interventions within a declared intervention class. Evaluation would specify in advance which changes are withheld, how accuracy is measured and which forms of generalization are being tested. This proposal follows the research motivation for intervention-aware benchmarks; its particular design is not an established standard.
completion_criteria.label: Predict held-out intervention outcomes from low-level observations under capped budgets

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: predictions would meet stated accuracy and uncertainty-coverage targets, accompanied by interval-width constraints or a proper scoring rule so that arbitrarily broad uncertainty intervals cannot pass. Evaluation would also test whether the learned abstractions support the relevant causal statements, rather than measuring outcome prediction alone. Recovery would be judged against an explicitly stated equivalence or abstraction criterion, not an unexplained requirement to reproduce a unique graph or human-readable variable names.
completion_criteria.label: Meet prediction accuracy, constrained uncertainty, and causal abstraction criteria

completion_criteria.text: Proposed external validation: a second demonstration would use a real laboratory system with independently checked intervention outcomes. The protocol would document the observation process, available actions, intervention costs and limits of the reference causal knowledge. Repeated runs and independent replication would assess whether performance survives different initial conditions and experimental instances. Pixel-level video quality and reward collected inside the training environment would be insufficient completion measures.
completion_criteria.label: Replicate intervention prediction performance in independently validated laboratory experiments

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: reports would state the systems, mechanisms and intervention families tested, where uncertainty remains informative, and where the method fails or must abstain. No numerical success threshold is established by the supplied evidence; targets would need justification for the intended use. Finite simulation and laboratory tests would demonstrate breadth across the tested conditions, not literal universality across all possible interventions or environments.
completion_criteria.label: Report tested intervention scope, informative uncertainty, and failure boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: MLC-01, A predictive theory of what deep networks learn, concerns explaining or predicting learning behavior; MLC-04 concerns whether a learned representation supports intervention predictions. MLC-06, Algorithmic legibility sufficient to verify and edit a model, overlaps through the need to inspect and assess representations, but causal predictive validity does not by itself make an entire model legible or editable. MLC-10, Non-vacuous behavioral certificates at frontier scale, connects through useful guarantees and uncertainty: finite intervention tests would not alone constitute a broad behavioral certificate.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-02, Domain learning at a human experience budget, overlaps through efficient use of observations and interventions, while MLC-04 specifies the causal capability those data must support. MLC-09, Skill learning from scarce, irreversible, real-world outcomes, adds practical constraints that simulated or resettable intervention tests do not capture. A causal world model could inform action selection under those constraints, but predicting outcomes and learning a successful real-world skill are distinct achievements.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-03, Cumulative learning without forgetting or loss of plasticity, concerns retaining and extending competence over time; a causal model could still forget mechanisms or become unable to learn new ones. MLC-07, Open-ended curricula that create externally verified new competencies, could supply learning challenges or experiments for a world model, but generating a curriculum does not establish intervention-faithful representations, and such representations do not automatically create open-ended competence.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-08, Discovery of new empirical laws, confirmed by experiment, is a possible downstream connection. MLC-04 could support experiment selection and prediction, whereas MLC-08 additionally requires a new empirical law and experimental confirmation. Only the roster title for MLC-08 is supplied, so this distinction is conceptual rather than a comparison against its full record.

Roster-based synthesis: MLC-05, Local credit assignment that matches backpropagation at scale, and MLC-11, Frontier competence at a biological-order power budget, concern how learning is implemented and resourced. Either could affect the feasibility of causal world models, but neither establishes their causal validity. Conversely, a successful MLC-04 demonstration would not establish local credit assignment or biological-order energy efficiency. These comparisons use the supplied roster titles, not independently reviewed records.

The concept also overlaps causal inference, model-based reinforcement learning and experimental design. Its distinctive combination is to learn the causal representation from low-level observations and validate prediction under unseen interventions. Planning with a learned dynamics model is a relevant component, but its causal scope must be established through appropriate intervention evidence.

brief.title: Models that predict what happens when we change things
possible: People could explore a proposed change in a simulator before trying it for real, including changes the simulator had never encountered. It would learn what matters from images, sounds or text and a limited number of experiments, within a defined range of changes.
why: Researchers could choose more informative experiments. Planners could compare actions and policies using predictions of their effects. People would no longer have to specify every cause-and-effect relationship by hand.

sources.showed: Their review connects learning from observations with predicting the effects of deliberate changes. It describes partial theoretical foundations and the challenge of discovering which features represent causes and effects.
sources.cited_for: The foundations for learning cause-and-effect relationships directly from sensory observations.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate the combined capability with limited experiments and previously unseen changes.

sources.showed: An earlier version of the same work.

sources.who: Danijar Hafner, Jurgis Pasukonis, Jimmy Ba and Timothy Lillicrap
sources.showed: Dreamer learned a model of its environment and used imagined futures to improve its actions. It outperformed specialized methods across over 150 tasks using a single configuration.
sources.quote: Here we present the third generation of Dreamer, a general algorithm that outperforms specialized methods across over 150 diverse tasks, with a single configuration.
sources.cited_for: Learned simulators can help an agent choose effective actions across diverse tasks.
sources.not_established: Task performance does not establish reliable predictions when previously unseen changes alter the system's mechanisms.

sources.showed: Their preprint reports human judgments of physical consistency in videos from ten generation models. The tested models performed poorly overall, and more detailed hints did not resolve the physics errors.
sources.quote: By incorporating progressively more concrete hints, naming the law and adding detailed mechanistic descriptions, we show that prompt refinement alone cannot overcome the models’ inability to generate physically coherent videos.
sources.cited_for: Visually convincing generation can still fail to respect physical laws.
sources.not_established: The benchmark does not test learning causes from observations or predicting the outcomes of changes withheld during training.

shown: Google DeepMind and University of Toronto researchers built Dreamer, which learns an internal simulator and improves its actions through imagined futures. It collected diamonds in Minecraft without human examples or a staged training curriculum.

Schölkopf and collaborators describe restricted theoretical results for learning causes and effects. These foundations and Dreamer's task performance establish parts of the capability; neither demonstrates the full combination.
missing: A combined demonstration must learn useful causes and effects from sensory data and predict unfamiliar changes with a limited experiment budget.
The learned features must connect available physical actions to the changes they represent, even when observations vary.
Laboratory tests must establish repeatable predictions and useful uncertainty when competing explanations fit the observations.

milestones.label: Accurate predictions of changes withheld during training
milestones.explanation: A simulated test would hide the system's mechanisms and require predictions from sensory data under a capped experiment budget and a declared class of changes. This would test whether learning extends to unfamiliar changes.

milestones.label: Accurate predictions with meaningful confidence and learned causes
milestones.explanation: Predictions would meet accuracy targets with uncertainty that is reliable without being too broad, and learned features would preserve relevant cause-and-effect distinctions. This would establish more than accurate guesses.

milestones.label: Independently replicated predictions in a laboratory
milestones.explanation: Laboratory experiments would independently confirm outcomes, with repeated runs and replication across starting conditions and experimental instances. This would test whether performance extends beyond simulation.

milestones.label: Clear limits on where predictions work
milestones.explanation: Results would define the tested systems and changes, where uncertainty remains useful, and when predictions fail or must be withheld. This would establish the range within which people could rely on the model.

uncertain: Which assumptions can distinguish competing causal explanations while still fitting realistic sensory data and limited experiments?
What experiment budgets, accuracy targets and uncertainty limits would make a decisive test, and which laboratory system would suit it?

page.title: Causal world models for unseen interventions
page.definition: A model learns causal variables and the rules connecting them from sensory observations under a fixed experimental budget. Within a specified class of interventions, it predicts the average measured outcome of a change whose value or combination of settings was absent from training. In a light tunnel, for example, it would predict the average sensor reading if a polarizer were turned to an untried angle.

goal.need: At one X-ray free-electron laser, a 2018 estimate put tuning at about 400 hours of beam time a year. Operators use past scans and beam physics to choose magnet settings. Hundreds of scans left some relationships between magnets unresolved. If the mechanisms learned from beam measurements still apply at untried settings, operators could compare the expected pulse energy of several magnet combinations before testing one, leaving more beam time for experiments.

figures.caption: Factor recovery by contrastive causal representation learning.
figures.note: Mean ± standard deviation over five random initializations, using 60,000 images per condition. The dimensionless score measures correlation between matched learned and ground-truth factors; higher is better.

completion.title: An independent laboratory replicates a learned model's predictions of unseen physical interventions.
completion.criterion: Learn causal variables and mechanisms from images of one physical system under a predeclared finite intervention budget. For every held-out intervention family, predict the mean of a prespecified measured outcome. Mean squared error on new experiments must be no greater than that of an independently validated physical model supplied the causal variables. An independent laboratory must repeat the entire learning-and-test procedure and satisfy the same inequality without increasing the budget. Test intervention values or combinations must be absent from training; causal-variable value labels cannot be training inputs.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external completion protocol covering the combined capability was located.
completion.basis: Searches covered DARPA causal-model programmes, NIST/ISO standards, prizes, causal-representation benchmarks and independent laboratory replication. No external test combined sensory learning, a bounded intervention budget and unseen physical interventions. The fallback is restricted to one physical system and mean outcomes. Its comparison with a validated physical model is an Atlas choice; no universal numerical budget or accuracy cutoff was located.

milestones.title: A model recovers a simulator's causal graph with zero structural Hamming distance.
milestones.criterion: Match learned variables to simulator variables using the feature-importance matrix for the disentanglement score. Compare the learned directed graph with the simulator graph after matching. Exact recovery requires zero edge additions, deletions or reversals. For the CausalCircuit protocol, train three random initializations on encodings of 512 × 512 RGB images and score the run with median validation loss.
milestones.set_by: Exact graph-recovery convention, operationalized by Brehmer et al. in Appendix D.1; the reported demonstration concerns the CausalCircuit simulator.
milestones.threshold_quote: We then compute the structural Hamming distance (or graph edit distance) between the learned graph and the true graph.

milestones.title: Shared optical inputs have R² near one and unshared inputs score lower for each tested view pair.
milestones.criterion: Use the light tunnel's 60,000 observations and the supplied selection of shared encoding coordinates. Pair the camera separately with the light and current measurements, the first angle sensor, and the second angle sensor. For each pair, fit nonlinear predictors of each true input from each view's shared encoding and average the two R² scores. Across five random initializations, shared inputs must score near one and unshared inputs significantly lower. The protocol gives no numerical tolerance or significance level.
milestones.set_by: Gamella, Bing and Runge, Section 3.2, Figure 5 and Appendix A.2.3 of the light-tunnel benchmark.
milestones.threshold_quote: a score near one for the factors in the content block and a significantly lower score for those in the style block.

milestones.title: A learned model matches a validated physical model's error on unseen interventions in one laboratory.
milestones.criterion: In one laboratory, learn causal variables and mechanisms from images of one physical system under a predeclared finite intervention budget, without causal-variable value labels as training inputs. Predict the mean of a prespecified measured outcome at intervention values or combinations absent from training. For each held-out family, the learned model's mean squared error on new experiments must be no greater than that of an independently validated physical model given the causal variables.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback after searching causal-representation and causal-chamber protocols; no published acceptance threshold for this combined physical demonstration was located.

milestones.title: A model predicts mean outcomes for 100 simulated interventions outside the training range.
milestones.criterion: Learn from 10,000 simulated observations with 10 measured features and d action coordinates, for d = 2, 4 and 10. Draw training actions uniformly from [−1, 1]ᵈ. Predict the mean outcome at 100 test actions drawn uniformly from [−3, −1]ᵈ. Report mean squared error against the simulator's true mean over 10 repetitions, alongside an action-only regression and a model given the true latent predictors. The protocol specifies no numerical error cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Saengkyongam and colleagues, Rep4Ex multidimensional extrapolation protocol, Appendix H.1 and Figure 7.
milestones.threshold_quote: we generate 100 test points of A from a uniform distribution

not_found: No independent laboratory replication combining sensory causal-variable learning and held-out physical intervention prediction was located.
No workshop or research-programme statement disputing the feasibility or value of the bounded physical prediction goal was located.
